title: Distributional Balancing with Machine Learning for Clinical Trial Augmentation Using Real-World Data
abstract: arXiv:2609.23524v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In clinical trials, randomization of treatment and control groups is typically used to ensure the groups have similar covariate distributions on average, resulting in unbiased causal effect estimation. Such balanced covariate distributions are hard to achieve in practice, however, due to recruitment costs, patient dropouts, and more. One possible solution to this problem is to include control patients from external, real world databases. In this paper, we propose DBML, a method that selects control units from a real world database by matching the distribution between the treatment group and the potential control group, instead of matching units between two groups. DBML has three steps. First, we detect anomalous database units (with respect to the treatment distribution) using a variational autoencoder. Second, we re-weight the remaining database units to match the distribution of the treatments. Finally, we use these weights to sample

translated_title: 基于机器学习的分布平衡方法：利用真实世界数据增强临床试验
translated_abstract: 在临床试验中，通常采用治疗组和对照组的随机化来确保两组在平均意义上具有相似的协变量分布，从而实现无偏的因果效应估计。然而，由于招募成本、患者退出等原因，这种平衡的协变量分布在实践中很难实现。解决该问题的一种可能方法是从外部的真实世界数据库中纳入对照患者。本文提出了DBML方法，该方法通过匹配治疗组与潜在对照组之间的分布（而非在两组之间进行单元匹配），从真实世界数据库中选择对照单元。DBML包含三个步骤：首先，我们使用变分自编码器检测数据库中相对于治疗分布的异常单元；其次，我们对剩余的数据库单元进行重新加权，以匹配治疗组的分布；最后，我们利用这些权重进行采样。
tldr: 本文提出DBML方法，通过变分自编码器检测异常单元并对数据库单元重新加权，使真实世界数据库中对照组的分布与治疗组分布相匹配，从而有效增强临床试验。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes DBML, a method that selects control units from real-world databases by detecting anomalies with a variational autoencoder and re-weighting units to match the treatment group's distribution, thereby augmenting clinical trials.
